title: Derived constant wait threshold on real data with constructed arrival delays, matched to the package generator

decision_rule.latency: Derived threshold p95 latency below Wait-if-uncertain p95 in all 7 rotations
decision_rule.errors: Derived threshold error count within the paired 95% interval of the Proposed policy in at least 5 of 7 rotations

notes: The delivered protocol assumed sigma_delay equal to sigma_forecast at 0.4 and set the delay of a not-late item to zero and its own note asked for both to be confirmed against the package and a new file frozen if they differed. They differ. core.py draws the delay as median 900 s times a lognormal of sigma 0.5 for a late item and uniform 0 to 30 s for one that is not late, then multiplies by a lognormal of sigma 0.4 for the forecast. This file matches the generator so that the real-data arm exercises the same delay family as the synthetic condition it is compared against. The late fraction 0.70, the median 900 s and the forecast sigma 0.4 were confirmed unchanged against config.json.
why_frozen: Frozen before the run; sha256 recorded beside it and in the run manifest. Seeds are CONFIG["seeds"] from upstream/prototype_v2.3/config.json, the same five the paper averages, so the unhandled column can be checked against the printed table. The rev1 protocol used [0,1,2,3,4] and could not reproduce it; see archive/superseded_2026-10-08/WHY_SUPERSEDED.txt.
